messages:
Diego: Heads-up: opened PR to update the exports guide with clearer SOC2-friendly language and a client-side pseudonymization example. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1499

docs-bot: CI: docs build started. Running linkcheck and sample code checks.

Alyssa: LGTM at a glance. Two small asks: 1) use the term 'pseudonymized' (not 'anonymized') throughout; 2) add a short FAQ Q/A about re-identification risk.

Ken: For the sample code, can we show a minimal Rust snippet (pseudocode) and a Python one? Legal liked HMAC examples earlier. Keep KMS calls as placeholders.

Security-Bot: Security note: examples should explicitly state keys/salts are customer-managed. Do not imply Redwood holds or manages customer salts by default.

Diego: Agreed. Draft sentence I plan to add: "Exported audit records may include pseudonymized identifiers derived from customer-controlled keys or salts; re-identification requires possession of those keys and is not performed by Redwood unless customers explicitly configure key sharing." Happy to tweak wording.

Alyssa: That reads well. Make the KMS pointer a link to /docs/security/key-management and add a one-line changelog under docs/changelog.md -> Security: clarify export pseudonymization wording + client examples.

Ken: Rust pseudocode (will include in PR):

```rust
// client-side pseudonymize example (pseudocode)
use hmac::{Hmac, Mac};
use sha2::Sha256;

fn pseudonymize(id: &str, key: &[u8]) -> String {
    let mut mac = Hmac::<Sha256>::new_from_slice(key).unwrap();
    mac.update(id.as_bytes());
    hex::encode(mac.finalize().into_bytes())
}

// key should come from customer-managed KMS; do not upload raw keys to Redwood.
```

Diego: Nice. I'll also add a Python snippet using hmac + hashlib and a brief JS SubtleCrypto example. Keeping all KMS interactions pseudocode.

docs-bot: CI: linkcheck failed - exports.md line 110 -> broken anchor (#residency-info).

Alyssa: That anchor was renamed in the restructure. I'll update the link to #data-residency-and-sovereignty in the PR.

Ken: One more thing: SOC2 reviewers asked for an explicit sentence about control boundary. Maybe add: "Redwood's role is to provide the export mechanism; control of cryptographic material used for pseudonymization remains with the customer unless explicitly configured otherwise."

Diego: Adding both lines. Pushed changes and fixed the anchor. Triggering CI.

docs-bot: CI: build passed on staging. Code-sample-check OK, linkcheck OK.

Alyssa: :tada: Quick review done. Please add the changelog entry and then merge.

Diego: Changelog added under docs/changelog.md and PR merged. Thanks all!

Security-Bot: Note: We'll surface this change to SOC2 reviewers in the next evidence bundle. No action required now.
